utterances.text: Witness, did you provide any statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 23rd of April, 1999, concerning events you witnessed in Djakovica, and specifically in Millosh Giliq, in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review your statement, recently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. We've read -- I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: From the review you made, were you able or did you have any corrections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There is a minor correction here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Can the witness please be given a document with ERN number K053.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it you're abandoning that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The witness doesn't have it in front of him, so I will take him quickly through the document to see the corrections he made.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, on the 24th of November, 2006, during the proofing session, do you remember making changes to the first sentence in paragraph 1, from the top of page 2 of the English version; instead of the word "in the evening," we should read "after midnight?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haider, we're told that the witness doesn't have the document. I don't know what that document is that you've given him, but unless it's -- it's okay, if it's his statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Pristina] He has been given, Your Honour, the declaration --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Pristina] He has been given the statement -- the translation in Albanian, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the position. Thank you. And can you turn the microphone again towards the witness or we'll not hear him. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Can I have an answer for the first question that I asked regarding your first sentence in paragraph 1 of the page 2, in both your English version and Albanian version. Instead of the word "evening," it should read "after midnight?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Witness, it's the very first sentence of the statement. It really doesn't matter, you know. It's clearly 12.25 a.m.. The only thing I wonder, now that you've raised the matter, is whether it's the 1st or the 2nd of April, which may be important.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: No, actually. I'm sorry, Your Honour. Maybe I was misunderstood. I meant the first sentence, and not the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The first sentence says about 12.25 a.m., which is just after midnight; and then it says the 1st of April. Now, is it in fact the 1st of April, or is there confusion about what the date is because there's a reference to evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was between the 1st and the 2nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's the 2nd of April. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, the fourth paragraph in your Albanian version, the third sentence, instead of "my mother," you wanted the statement to read "stop mothers and asked questions about where their sons were and what were they doing." That is what you intended, instead of "stop my mother and ask her questions where I was and what I was doing." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. I wanted to say "mothers," in general; women.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Moving to paragraph 9, which will be on the third -- will be on the second page of your Albanian version. The second sentence from the top "only those mentioned in the statement were killed and not all residents of that home." Is that correction correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Can you ask the question once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: On page 2 of the Albanian version, paragraph 9 from the top, you would like to change your sentence from "those mentioned in the statement were killed and not all residents of that home." That's the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Moving to page 3 of the English version, which is also page 3 of the Albanian version, the second sentence in paragraph 5 from the top, "people were staying in the basement of this house." That is what you wanted to say, instead of "people staying in this house." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: The second sentence in paragraph 5 from the top, "people were staying in the basement of this house." That is what you wanted to say, and not "people staying in this house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: People were staying in the basements, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: The next sentence is the second sentence in paragraph 7 from the top, "in our neighbourhood." That is what you intended to say, instead of "within this town." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: The last sentence in paragraph 8 from the top of page 3 English version and page 3 Albanian version, "to ask mothers about their sons and where they were," instead of "my mother about me and where I was." Is that the correction you intended to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Page 4 of the English version, page 4 Albanian version, last sentence in paragraph 1 from the top, "mostly Albanian," instead of "like rabbits." Is that the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Page 5 English version, page 5 Albanian version, under number 11 when you started to mention the names of perpetrators; number 11, "Popadic Nenad worked with electricity state company in Djakovica, instead of"the director with electricity state company." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Under number 12, "Stanimir Aksic," instead of last name unknown. Is that the correct change you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Under number 13, "Laza Nedeljkovic," instead of last name unknown. Is that the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It's Nedeljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Is that the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Under number 14, "Novica Nedeljkovic," instead of last name unknown. Is that the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. Nedeljkovic is the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Under number 15, "Miomir Nedeljkovic," instead of last name unknown. Is that the correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, Nedeljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: The last correction is on page 5 to page 6 of English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you go to that, have I rightly understood that two of these names were changed to Nedeljkovic and one was changed to Nadakovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: No. All three of them were changed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. No, let's -- can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nedeljkovic is the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at number 13 again, please, Witness, and tell me what the name of Laza, what is his second name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Laza Nedeljkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies a mistake in the transcript earlier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: The last correction, second sentence in the last paragraph from the top of page 5 to the last sentence on top of page 6, "I saw -- hang" should be taken out. Do you intend to take those sentences out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 5, the last sentence up to page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I gather that the picture going from here to Pristina has been lost and that we probably need to break. But it would be helpful to me, certainly, when we come back if you were to ask some questions to explain how on earth that sort of information gets into this statement, and now has to be withdrawn from it, bearing in mind the extremely sensitive nature of that information. So we'll adjourn until this technical hitch has been resolved. I'm told roughly ten minutes. --- Break taken at 11.47 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I gather the problem has been resolved and we can now be seen again, so please continue with your examination, Mrs. Neema.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to have a look at your statement, the Albanian version, page 5, the second paragraph after the names. Are you there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You haven't asked a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: No, no. I just wanted him to get to the page and the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. Do you have a question for him?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, could we please pose the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, during the proofing --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: During the proofing on the 24th of November, 2006, you indicated that you would like the third sentence up to the last sentence in that paragraph to be taken out. Would you explain to the Court as to why you want that statement to be taken out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Which part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Witness, could you listen to me, please. What you're being asked is why you wish to remove from your statement the following words: "I saw blood at the door of the Cana house, where Shpresa Cana had been shot. The body had been removed. I went to the Deda home, where I saw the body of the 5 year old, Argjend Ylber Demjaha, who had been hanged." Now, why do you want to remove that from your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it's not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Neema.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, have you heard what the Judge has just read to you? Why do you want that piece of information taken out of your statement? Is there any reason?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that question has been answered; he said it is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: What is not accurate in that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It is not accurate. I don't remember to have said this. I know that I have said that they killed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Apart from the corrections you made, you have gone through your statement, are there any other corrections you want to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. When it says Mentor Deda was hanged, I didn't say this. I said that he was killed in the yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that takes us back to page 2 in the English, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: But did you see him when he was killed, or you heard it from other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. Mentor Deda -- I heard that Mentor Deda is dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you also hear how he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mentor went to take his family in his home, when from the window -- from the wall he saw that they were killed. And then he said, "Argjend has been killed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mentor Deda, the uncle of the dead son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Neema, I can tell you I am deleting the words "who was hanged" from my statement on page 2. It doesn't seem to be something the witness can support.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Prosecution wish to -- this statement which was taken on the 23rd of April, 1999, which is Exhibit P02517 to be admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And we pray this to be admitted under seal, and we will file a redacted version for the public use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again by Friday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, were you born and raised in Djakovica along Rruga Millosh Giliq street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: When you were growing up, did you as well grow up with Serb children in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: By April 1999, were these Serbs still living in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: What was the relationship like between the Serbs and Kosovo Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We had good relations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Was there any time when this relationship changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Talking about my neighbourhood, I may say that we never had any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: In your statement, you gave us an account of what took place after midnight on the 1st -- on the 2nd of April, 1999. You also gave us the name of Serb perpetrators whom you allege committed crimes. When did this start or how did this start, if the relationship was good all along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The crimes occurred between the 1st and the 2nd of April at 12.25.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Was that the only time these Serbs committed those crimes or any crimes which occurred in your street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: You also stated in your statement that your property was burned. Was your property burned the very night you were talking about in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Did you see who committed that crime, who burned your property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And also in your statement, you talked about other properties which were burned, including that of Lulezim Vejsa. Do you know who burned those properties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: According to what all the people in our neighbourhood knew, they were burned by the Serbs, from our neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Who are those people in your neighbourhood? Does that include you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. I'm one of the people in my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Now I would like to take you to the names you mentioned in your statement. The names mentioned in your statement include Pitulic Novak, Milos Scepanovic, Gajo Scepanovic, Milan Scepanovic, Mile Scepanovic, Tihomir Raicevic, Ljubisa Raicevic, Misko Raicevic, Sasa Raicevic, Nenad Raicevic, Popadic Nenad, Stanimir Nedeljkovic, Laza Nedeljkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Stanimir Aksic is absent, I think..

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Stanimir Aksic, Laza Nedeljkovic, Novica Nedeljkovic, and Miomir Nedeljkovic. Are these among those Serbs who burned down property that belongs to Kosovo Albanians in your street or in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. The entire neighbourhood testifies to these persons; I am one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Now, specifically focusing on you, did you see any of these people you mentioned burning any of the property on Millosh Giliq or in your neighbourhood? Not necessarily your property, any property in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: What made you say or what made you mention them? Personal experience, you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: These persons searched our neighbourhood until the moment when it was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: When you say they searched your neighbourhood, what do you mean? Can you explain to the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I said they had the neighbourhood under control.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what you mean by, "they had the neighbourhood under control."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We didn't see any other Serbs other than those who lived in our neighbourhood. We constantly saw the Serbs living in our neighbourhood, and all the neighbourhood knows that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Were these the only Serbs living in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There were other Serbs, but they lived in another part. I am talking of my neighbourhood where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: In your statement -- I'm taking you back to your statement. In your statement, you allege that the Serbs who committed these crimes were wearing a uniform. Can you explain to the Court what kind of uniform these people who committed these crimes were wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: They were wearing police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Can you describe those police uniforms. What do you mean by police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm perplexed, and so I don't know whether it's really an objection or whether I'm missing something here. My understanding of what the witness has testified to here today is that he did not see any crimes being committed, and now he's being asked to describe the uniforms of the persons who committed crimes. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think we have to read the statement and what he's now saying, which clearly qualifies much of page 4, together --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree. But I'm confused now by the sworn testimony he's given in court that he didn't see any crimes being committed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. What we're now moving to is something I think that is perfectly capable of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question, though, I think, Mrs. Neema, would be better formulated as referring to the people who had the neighbourhood under control, and then there won't be any doubt about the situation. So, Witness, you're being asked to explain -- sorry, describe the police uniforms that you referred to being worn by the people you say were in control of your neighbourhood. Could you do that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: What kind of blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Is there any other group which you know that wore that kind of uniform or that kind of blue you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. I'm talking of the uniform we saw them wearing at the time, and usually this is uniform worn by the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: What do you mean by "reservists?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: They were not regular police.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Do you want to tell that the uniform they were -- the reservists were wearing was different from what the police was wearing? What made you believe these were reservists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: They worked elsewhere. They worked in other places. They didn't go to school to become policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And among those you saw had control of your neighbourhood and wearing these reservists uniform, were those you mentioned in your statement among those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Neema, I may be speaking for myself when I ask you how this fits with what's actually in the statement about what they were wearing. The Prosecution has surely got to present some sort of consistent account from a witness before we can be expected to get down to the job of analysing just how much of it we accept or reject. But if we're going to get entirely inconsistent versions in writing and orally, there's got to be some attempt made to bring them into line or abandon the point. As it stands, these two versions are not consistent with each other. I'm very cautious not to say that where there's some means of reconciling them obvious in what's before us, but at the moment we could not conceivably reconcile these two versions, at least that's my opinion. I don't know if the other Judges agree, but I would be in enormous difficulty trying to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to bring the witness, I mean, in line so that I can get out of him what I'm -- the Prosecution intends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's quite -- that that's quite the right approach. The Prosecution has obviously to elicit from the witness his evidence, but there may come a point when you have to say a witness is so inconsistent that we just do not wish to rely on him. You may not be at that stage yet; and if you're not you're, then going to have to do something to give us a picture that we could possibly rely on, which at the moment doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: I'll try one more time, Your Honour. Your Honour, can I consult my colleagues for five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give us a moment to consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you wishing us to adjourn to enable you to do this, or are you wishing just simply to do it in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like a short adjournment if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think a short adjournment is possible now, we're going to have to have a lunch break. If I could have the indulgence of the interpreters, we could resume at half past 1.00. It may not be possible. I need to find out if they can accommodate that or not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm told that they can. So what we'll do now is adjourn until half past 1.00. Witness, there is going to be an interruption now in your evidence. We will also use the interruption to have our lunch break, so we will be breaking for an hour. Meanwhile, it is very important that you have no discussion with anybody at all about your evidence. You can discuss with other people anything else you want, but not the evidence you are giving or will give in this courtroom. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll resume at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Shall we resume the evidence now?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Witness K74, we will now continue with your evidence, and Mrs. Neema will continue her examination. Mrs. Neema.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to take you a little bit back in your testimony. On the night of 1st of April, 1999, what was your neighbourhood like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: On the 1st of April, until 12.25, we didn't have electricity, darkness prevailed all over; and at 12.25, we started hearing shots and then the burning and the killings and these things started.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And when that started, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I was at the basement of a neighbour; Gezim Nagafci is his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: While in that basement, could you hear anything; and if yes, what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, because our houses are along the road; all the houses that were burned. We heard noises. We heard also Albanian being spoken, but at that time we were there behind because fire was spreading all over.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Was there -- during that night, was there any time you came out of the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: You are asking me if I went out of the basement?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Yes, that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In the basement, there were the children and the women; whereas, us, the adults, we were standing. They were lying down. We were standing around the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: While standing around the yard, were you able to see people moving up and down the street, or was it quiet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. You couldn't see anyone because there are houses that prevent the view, and it was total darkness, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: In your statement you talked about people you believe committed the crime. When did you hear or feel their presence on the streets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: When they started setting fire at 12.25, we were sheltered, about 200, 300 people there; then we heard Albanian being spoken. They called out every house owner in Albanian in a loud voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Was there any time when you came out of the basement and see these people who were burning the houses which you allege were burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. I didn't see the houses burning, but the entire neighbourhood saw those people roaming the streets of the neighbourhood some days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And after that event of houses being burned, whether it was on the 1st of April -- particularly, the 1st of April to the 2nd of April, was there any time you saw these people or anybody you believe committed this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, no. I'm saying I didn't see them. We were behind the place where the fire was set. And we ran to save ourselves and the children, and we gathered at a garden behind the house. We stayed there in the basement until around 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Let me take you a little bit back again. When you are talking about these people you allege burned your houses or houses on Millosh Giliq, and you say when they came to the street they started calling and speaking in Albanian, were you able to hear what were they saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We heard in Albanian, because we were there for 45 years, living together, and we knew each other very well. And they called on every one by name and asked them to open the door, and they wanted to commit provocations. But we fled and, as I said, we were gathered about 200, 300 people in that place, in garden.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: This morning, I asked you about the names you mentioned in your statement. Apart from you mentioning the names, you said everybody else in the neighbourhood knew that these people were the ones who committed those crimes. How did you or your neighbours came to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I said so because after we went to Albania, even before we went to Albania, each of us was saying, "God, what our neighbours, our Serbian neighbours did to us. They killed us. They destroyed us."

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: How did you know that they killed you or destroyed you? What made you believe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We came to this conclusion because before the occurrence of the 1st and 2nd April happened, they were committing acts of thefts in towns and villages, bringing home television sets and other appliances in that place of Lubisha Raicevic. And the entire neighbourhood saw this happening because they couldn't sleep all night out of here and kept watch, seeing what was going on in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Apart from those you mentioned -- people you mentioned in your statement, were there any other people who were knew to that neighbourhood or whom, before the 1st of April, you saw in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We saw them all the time, these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: And what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Nothing. They came back from work, carrying automatic rifles, coming in, going out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, first will be counsel for General Lukic, and thereafter we'll follow the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I am one of the attorneys for Mr. Sreten Lukic. And I would beg your indulgence to pay close attention to the questions that I have for you, so you can provide me with the answers that are most accurate. And we can move through this as efficiently as possible, but now I have to focus on some things in your statement and in your testimony today to try and clear up some things. Now, first of all, am I correct that you did not personally eye-witness any of the acts of arson or killing that you identify in your statement; that is to say, you did not personally see the perpetrators of these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I take it then the pages in your statement - it's in the English the bottom of page 3, the bottom of page 4, the middle of page 5. Sir, the transcript shows that your answer is "no" to my question. Is it no, that you did not see the perpetrators or no, I am not correct? Let's clear that up first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. I didn't see the perpetrators of the crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on page 3, let's go through these each one at a time. On page 3 of your statement it says, at the bottom the last paragraph in the English. "I had been staying in the basement of the neighbour of mine. For short periods, I would go to my property and look to see what was happening. The people doing this burning and killing were Serbs from the neighbourhood." So am I to take it then, sir, that this part of your sworn statement is actually incorrect? Sir, can we have a response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Is it possible for you to repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. I'm trying to see if there's other corrections that need to be made to your sworn statement that is being introduced into evidence. At page 3, the bottom of page 3, the statement says: "I had been staying in the basement of the neighbour of mine. For short periods, I would go to my property and look to see what was happening. The people doing this burning and killing were Serbs from the neighbourhood." And I'm asking you, sir, are we to understand that this part of your statement needs to be corrected, that you did not actually see the people doing the burning and killing were Serbs from the neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: According to the information from the neighbourhood -- of the people from the neighbourhood, everybody was saying that these Serbs killed us, burned us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you then for the basis of another one of your statements at page 4, the paragraph before you start listing the names of some 16 individuals. In there, your sworn statement that you signed says: "Since the very first night of NATO bombing, they were patrolling the streets, holding hand-held lamps, and sending signals to each other. Some of the men who did the burning had painted faces, blackened. They were wearing bullet-proof vests and camouflage green uniforms. The men that I saw do this burning and killing include the following men that I know and recognise. I saw them drinking at the pool hall owned by Luli, near Luli's compound. They were in uniform at that time." Sir, is it your testimony here today that you did not in fact see these 18 individuals that you have named wearing camouflage green uniforms and participating in the burning and killing of that night? Is this part of your statement incorrect as well? Or is any part of it correct? I mean -- if there is part of it that you do know and you did see, please let me know. I'm just trying to figure out what I have to work with here in terms of material.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I saw them holding flash-lights for several nights before. I saw them giving signals to each other and surveying the neighbourhood. That night, too, we -- often they made signs with these flash-lights. They set fire to the buildings of the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you actually see them set these fires, these 18 individuals that are now named at page 4 and 5 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I told you no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I told you we saw them and I saw them some days ago, some nights ago making signals to each other with these flash-lights.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did -- just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you, on the night of the 1st and 2nd of April, see these individuals with flash-lights making signs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That night, no. But we could see the lights of the flash-lights at the doors of our yards, and it was about 10.00, 10.30; and at 12.25, they set fire to the houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did the light that they cast and the way that the lights were used look any different on the night of the 1st and 2nd of April from the earlier nights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the previous nights they used hand-held flash-lights. The Serbs -- the Serbian houses were across each other, 40, 50 metres from one another, and they made signals to each other; whereas, the night I'm talking about the light cast was huge light, directed at our houses, and it was 10.30 in the evening. And at 12.25, they started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to focus on the two remaining points there in this section that we had just read. First of all, in this section you refer to these men as wearing bullet-proof vests and camouflage green uniforms. Later in your statement at page 6, you identify another person, Milos Scepanovic, and you say he was also in the same green camouflage uniform worn by the Serbs described above. Is that correct? Did these individuals when you saw them on the night in question, around 10.30 in the evening or before, wear camouflage green uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I said that they had green police --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- blue police uniform every time we saw them. Even before they set fire to the houses, we saw them wearing this kind of uniform. Milos Scepanovic was active in the police ranks. The others were reservists from the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, the question I have for you then is: Why is it that your entire statement, which you earlier today verified you had read, gone over, and were confirming to be true and accurate, only states that the persons who did all this were wearing green camouflage uniforms. Why has your testimony here changed today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't think this is in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm reading from the statement, Exhibit P2517. I don't know if you have that there in front of you, but the paragraph starts: "Since the very first night of NATO bombing," it's on page 4 exactly in the middle of the page, "they were wearing bullet-proof vests and camouflage green uniforms." The statement in question was taken on the 23rd of April, 1999, less than a month after the event in question. Was your recollection of the event better a few weeks after the event or today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: This I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think that your recollection of the events was better in April of 1999 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Of course, in 1999 my recollection was better, but we were also under trauma. We were traumatised at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can ask you about the next part of that same paragraph, since hopefully you're on that same page still. It says there: "I saw them drinking at the pool hall owned by Luli, near Luli's compound." Is this referring to the night in question? Did you see these 18 or so individuals drinking at the pool hall owned by Luli?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I didn't say about that night, and I didn't say that every night they drank and they went to this pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, when did you see them drinking, if not that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: They went there regularly. I told you they kept the neighbourhood under their thumb. They went to shops, they drank. They did everything they wanted in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right, sir. I'd like to ask you about the page prior to this on page 3 of your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1999. And, again, at about the middle of the page in the English, it should be around there in the Albanian as well, the paragraphs are not numbered, it says: "About one or two hours prior to the burning of the houses, they lit the area with spotlights. A number of Serbs from the neighbourhood were standing in front of Lulezim Vejsa's pool hall, which is adjacent to his compound. The Serbs were standing in uniform drinking. They also had men in a high building at the end of the street maintaining a lookout on the street. Children could hear what these men were saying as they were drinking." Now, how does this -- how do you reconcile this testimony from your sworn written statement that seems to contradict what you just told me a moment ago? Do you have an answer for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question and tell me where to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is page 3 of the English. I'm trying to find the exact reference in Albanian, as we speak. It is right after the paragraph where you talk about the 50 to 60 people staying at the house of Njazi Parashuti, that you told them to leave. It is the next paragraph that starts: "About one or two hours prior to the burning of the houses, they lit the area with spotlights. A number of Serbs from the neighbourhood were standing in front of sitting Lulezim Vejsa's pool hall, which is adjacent to his compound. The Serbs were standing in uniform drinking. They also had men in a high building at the end of the street maintaining a lookout on the street. Children could hear what these men were saying as they were drinking." This part of your statement indicates that you saw these Serbs from your neighbourhood drinking in front of Lulezim Vejsa's pool high school, specifically on the night in question one or two hours prior to the burning of the houses, which is something you just told me is not correct. So please help me understand which is the true account of what you know. What can I rely upon to be the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I told you some days ago; I didn't say that night. I told you some days before, I saw them regularly walking around the neighbourhoods, going where they wanted, drinking. They could do what they wanted; we couldn't because we were shut in our houses. And I'm not talking about the night of the event when the burning and the killing started.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then, sir, how do you explain the fact that this statement, which you took great pains to correct for the Prosecution, listing some ten to 12 corrections, explicitly states that this event that you saw of the drinking was one or two hours prior to the burning of the houses? Especially, if you read the next paragraph which says: "They were using a minivan/wagon-type vehicle to ram the gates of the properties and to break into the courtyards. The people involved in these attacks were Serbs we had grown up with in this neighbourhood." You specifically corrected this for the Prosecution to say "neighbourhood" instead of "town." So you read this with the Prosecutor and corrected it, and it still says that you saw people on the night in question and that these people were the local Serbs who were drinking in front of Lulezim Vejsa's pool hall. Please explain for me how this can be, if you are now telling me that you never saw it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where does it say he saw it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the statement page 3, it's the two middle paragraphs in the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where does it say he saw that, and he's not giving a hearsay account?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess that is a possible explanation if this entire statement is hearsay, then obviously we'll have another matter to discuss. But this is a section that he corrected for the Prosecution, so I would have expected if he didn't see it he would have changed it like the other things that he didn't see that were taken out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It seems to me, Mr. Ivetic, you're not making allowances for the witness's understanding of the process that we're engaged in and his capacity to take in the sort of question that you seem intent upon addressing to him. I think far simpler questions might clarify the position for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try to simplify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this part of your statement that says: "A number of Serbs from the neighbourhood were standing in front of Lulezim Vejsa's pool hall." Why did you put that in your statement? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not going to -- don't answer that, please. That's not going to help us because he's already told us -- just a minute, please. He's already told us that on previous nights he's seen people in uniform outside the pool hall. He said they were in control of the neighbourhood and so on. Your concern is about something else, as I understand it, which is what happened on the night of the burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which is in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. But your question doesn't make that clear. Your question could be easily answered on the basis that it was on previous nights. It's the earlier bit that you're really concerned about, in fact, the first four or five words of the [indiscernible] part, which I think needs to be built into your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, your statement says: "About one or two hours prior to the burning of the houses, they lit the area with spotlights. A number of Serbs from the neighbourhood were standing in front of Lulezim Vejsa's pool hall, which is adjacent to his compound." What is the basis of your including this in your sworn statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: These are the same people who the neighbours and the neighbourhood saw walking around the streets regularly controlling it; that is not only me who says this, the entire people of the neighbourhood say this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But what is your basis for saying it in your sworn statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is your basis for making these statements? I'm not yet concerned about what other people's basis are; I'm concerned about why you put this in your statement. Based upon what, did you have this knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I'm saying this on the basis of the fact that several days before when there were electricity cuts, these people were regularly seen with torch-lights, these that I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to page 5, after the list of 18 individuals that you identify as being somehow involved in these events, your statement says: "I heard the locks of the gates of Lulezim Vejsa's house being shot by these men. I saw and heard this procedure many times. It almost became routine, as they conducted this action in our neighbourhood on the properties described above. I heard the minivan hitting the gates of Luli's compound. I heard the noise of the gates being rammed; and then later after they entered, I saw Luli's house bursting in flames." Is any of this based upon what you really saw with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In the first sentence, you can read "I heard," not "I saw." We were in one house because our houses had been burnt. We were sheltering in that house. We were sheltering our children, while we, the adults, were following what was going on. We couldn't see what was going on, but we could hear shootings. We could hear them breaking down the doors. I don't know if they used cars to break these doors, but we could hear the noise of the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Witness K74, your statement says,"I saw Luli's house bursting in flames." Did you actually see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw every house that was burned. We were sheltering behind our houses, and we could see each and every house as it was set in flames. We were only 150 metres or 200 metres far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, sir, please let -- please give us information. Were you in the yard of the house where you were sheltering at, or were you in the basement? Because you've said both things today, and I'd like to find out which is accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In the basement. We were there sheltering up to the moment when the houses started to burn. From that moment, we left with our families, the entire neighbourhood, and sheltered behind our houses. And there we stayed until 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that there was no electricity that night, that it was dark around midnight, between April the 1st and April the 2nd, 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: On a regular basis, the electricity cuts were made at 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was that true for this night as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: As I said, we didn't have electricity after 7.00 p.m. for months. They would cut the power at 7.00, and we would no longer have electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. This list of 18 people, did you prepare this list, or did other people help you to prepare this list of 18 persons who you say are responsible for the crimes that you didn't see but heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Everyone in my neighbourhood saw something and knows something that happened to another person, and the entire neighbourhood compiled this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So this written statement that you have provided is actually not your testimony, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: This is our statement from every person from my neighbourhood, because we all suffered in that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your responses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Neema, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Witness, when you were asked about the houses being burned in the area, you stated that you and your family and other people went and hide behind the building. From where you were hiding, could you still see the flames going up of those houses which were being burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: You were also asked whether you were hiding in the basement all the time, because in your statement you indicated that there were a time you were also going out and specifically to your property and seeing what has happened to your property. Is that the correct version that there were times you were in the basement, and there were times you were going to see -- to your property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: My house was quite close. I could see it even from the basement. It was only two metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Last question: While you were in the basement, and you were saying your house was very close to where other incidents were taking place, were you in a position to hear any sounds or any voices of people talking or exchanging words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: While you were in the hiding in the basement, was it possible for you to hear what was going on on the outside or hear voices or people talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It was very calm, and I could hear everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEEMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: K74, that completes your evidence. Thank you very much for coming to give evidence to the Tribunal. You are now free to page 79 leave, and we will disconnect the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, does that complete your evidence for today, or are we ready to start the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are ready to start the next witness. Ms. Dragulev will lead that witness, if you would like to begin. I don't know if in light of the unanticipated break we had earlier when and where you were going to have another break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think we probably can't have one. We're limited to finishing at 3.00 because of the way the things have gone. Perhaps I could have an indication from the interpreters of the position, but I assume starting at half past 1.00 that we would finish at 3.00. Is that the interpreters' understanding also?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. We can, however, try to make some progress on what's to happen for the rest of the week. When we had the break, it was difficult to make plans not knowing how this last witness would progress. It now appears that Dusan Loncar would be available tomorrow, but I think the real difficulty is that it's not possible to set up a link for tomorrow. To try to accommodate the situation, the suggestion has been made - and I simply repeat the suggestion, which for once wasn't my idea - that we start at 7.30 on Friday because we have certain limitations. But I suspect that that could be difficult, even the attendance of the accused on time might be a problem. It's difficult for many people, I suspect, to make it for then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know what the witness's availability is at that time either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that must be a possibility because there is an hour's time difference, isn't there? Oh, no, it is the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the time the same, Mr. O'Sullivan? Yes. And the indications are that the examination of that witness could take more than a day, in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I've seen those indications, but I would raise a point that I think you addressed president witness Zyrapi to some extent. If that cross-examination goes into the point of presenting the Defence case as going merely beyond cross-examination, then I would say let's limit it to cross-examination of what's produced on direct. And if they want to call him as a witness in their case, there will certainly be an opportunity to do that later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, from what I've read, a large amount of it is the Defence case anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'd like to think it's both, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm saying is a part of it is clearly helpful to the Defence case. If the Defence sought to build on that, I would have thought that there was quite a strong argument for hearing that evidence at this point in time, bearing in mind the witness's health and bearing in mind that it is open to us to assign the time to the presentation of the positive Defence case. So...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that point, Your Honour, but I also understand the Defence had quite a concern about his health, which is legitimate. I know he told me he is scheduled to go to the spa, or whatever it is, for his rehabilitation next week. Perhaps it would be better if we didn't spend eight hours with him and only spent four or five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps we should all go to the spa and take the evidence there. Yes. In any event, that's a matter we, no doubt, can address shortly after we conclude today, because it may be that -- well, let me just ascertain one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the efforts will be made to see -- again to see if tomorrow or any part of tomorrow is a possibility. Then we'll address the question if the evidence is confined to Friday, how long that evidence is to be. And we shall now take the next witness. Ms. Dragulev. Who is the next witness so that we can get matters going?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Hysni Kryeziu and his evidence relates to paragraphs 72(b) and 77. [Trial Chamber and legal officer confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the efforts will be made to see -- again, to see if tomorrow or any part of tomorrow is a possibility; then we'll address the question if the evidence is confined to Friday, how long that evidence is to be. And we shall now take the next witness. Ms. Dragulev. Who is the next witness so that we can get matters going?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Hysni Kryeziu and his evidence relates to paragraphs 72(b) and 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the information of the Court page 82 we have one of our interns sitting in with us and that's Caroline Velte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kryeziu. Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the card which will now be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I read it in Albanian, may I? I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please be seated. Ms. Dragulev.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kryeziu. Could you please state your first and last name for the record.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: My name is Hysni Kryeziu.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated the 14th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And did you make a correction to that statement on the 19th of September, 2004?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes, I did. May I speak in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Certainly. You may have the wrong channel, I think, on the earphones.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review these statements during our proofing session?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Is the translation in Albanian now, Mr. Kryeziu?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And during our proofing session, after you had reviewed these statements, did you make some minor corrections or discover some translation errors?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: May I please ask the usher to provide the witness with an Albanian copy of his statement that has numbered paragraphs. Your Honours, we also made copies of the English statements that contain numbered paragraphs and the statements in B/C/S with numbered paragraphs so it's easier to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: The first correction you made, Mr. Kryeziu, was to paragraph 1 of your statement, the place -- your place of birth. Where were you born, Mr. Kryeziu?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Reti, Rahovec municipality on the 12th of April, 1949.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You also clarified that Dusanovo is a neighbourhood of the city of Prizren. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes. It is like a neighbourhood of Prizren town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You then made a correction to paragraph 2 of the statement where it says that your younger son Agron Kryeziu was exercising -- training with the KLA just for a few days later, for a few days last year. You explained to us that he actually went to a KLA training camp in order to register with the KLA, but that he was rejected by the KLA. So he was never actually a member of the KLA and never wore a KLA uniform. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes. He never wore a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. The next correction was to paragraph 7, where you talk about Haki Cuni. In this paragraph, you mention that you learned that he had been killed; but in fact later on, you learned that he was not killed, that he was tortured and maltreated, but that he was still alive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: In paragraph 9 in the middle of the paragraph, you mention that Scekic wore a black nylon stocking in his head, and you corrected the colour of the nylon stocking to light brown, sort of skin colour. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you say paragraph number 9?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 9, in the middle of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: It was possibly a mistranslation. The stocking he had on his head was not black but was brown. Others had black stockings on their heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same paragraph you refer to your brother, and you explained to us that he was physically disabled.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes. He was handicapped. He had lost one of his legs. When the Serb forces entered with tanks, APCs, and soldiers, there were people killed. We were beaten up and tortured; and about 500 metres far from my house near the house of Milan Scekic, who was chief of police, I don't know to which sector, he was in a Golf 2 make vehicle with his family. We had two women who were refugees from Bellacerka village staying with us. Scekic stopped us. He was in the company of others, as well. I asked him, "Commander, I ask you to leave one of the vehicles to me. You see that this person is handicapped." And he answered, "Don't talk too much. You will be executed in a second." At that moment, some soldiers came. They were wearing Chetnik caps, as we called them. They took out a knife, a big knife, and threatened us. They told me to leave the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kryeziu. I will just ask you to stop here for a moment. We just have one more correction to go through in the statement, and then we'll get back to your statement in a short while. Thank you. I believe the last correction you made was actually only a correction in the Albanian statement. In paragraph 12 of the statement, you refer to your neighbour Nebi Bucaj, his two sons. And it should state his brother-in-law had been executed by the Serb police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes. But on the way I heard from a woman - she was not neighbour of Nebi. I was Nebi's neighbour. Our houses are adjacent to one another - I could see from my house when he was stopped. I could hear the shootings coming from all sides. I heard that Nebi Bucaj, with his two sons and someone who was visiting in his house were killed, but not the brother. I don't remember saying that the brother was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: But it was -- do you remember saying that it was the brother-in-law, that his two sons and the brother-in-law? Is that a correction you made?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: No. I said a visitor. I don't know who he was. I know that he was from Randobrava village. This is what I heard later, actually, because I never knew that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, very much, sir. It was a visitor, not his brother-in-law. Now, taking those corrections into account, are your statements true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: The statement is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And can you confirm to this Court that that evidence is what you would give under oath today if you were asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: I will testify to everything that I've seen with my own eyes and everything is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would like to tender Exhibit 2514, the first one dated 14th May 1999, and the one dated 19 September 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 19 September 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: It is a correction to the Albanian statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which we now know is an inaccurate correction. Is that the one? Or is the yet another -- I only have the 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can provide you another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that is all the witness has spoken to, has he not?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I asked him if he gave another statement. I have a copy here, if you would like to see that. It's one correction to the number of houses in Dusanovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. I was aware of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu, you refer to policemen and to soldiers in your statement. Can you please explain to the Court how you were able to distinguish between the two.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes. The policemen had blue uniforms, dark blue; solid colour and camouflage pattern. The soldiers, on the other hand, had also plain-colour uniform, the SMB uniform as we call it, and some others had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Could I please have Exhibit P1325 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu, in your statement you mention that on the 20th of March, 1999, great numbers of police and Serb military surrounded the village with tanks and armoured vehicles. Please take a look at the photographs on the screen, that are displayed on the screen, and please tell us whether you recognise any of the vehicles that you refer to in your statement. Please note that there is more than one page, so please wait with your answer until you've seen all of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: The police APCs were these on photograph 2. They had smaller tanks, while the soldiers' tanks were bigger.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu, may I please ask you to look at the photographs first, before you give your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Can I have the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 6, these are the tanks that they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And I think, yes, can we have photograph number 3 -- page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were vehicles as those in number 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes, the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And number 14, and many others. And I cannot describe every type of vehicles because many years have passed, and there have been really many types of vehicles and APCs.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kryeziu. I have no further questions for you at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours no further questions at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour it will be General Lukic, General Lazarevic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, Mr. Sainovic, and Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Page 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Kryeziu. My name is Lukic, and I appear here for General Lukic. I would like briefly to come back to your statement. On page 85, line 11, in your testimony you described the caps worn by the people you saw, and you call them Chetnik-style caps. Could you tell us, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: They are black caps. We call them "Shajkaca." They have the Chetnik sign on them, and I remembered Draza Mihajlovic as soon as I saw these types of head-gear. They all were masked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you say they also had Chetnik emblems on those caps. Did you mean cockades?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they did not wear regular caps with regular emblems on their heads, the kind worn by ordinary policemen -- [In English] and military personnel, not only policemen?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: No. There were no regular caps, but these were the Chetnik caps with cockades. These were the caps, and they were wearing those on top of the nylon stockings, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: And I also saw some who had the sign Beli Orlovi, White Eagles, written.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw the emblems of White Eagles around on the uniforms or on the caps?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: On the uniforms of the army, on the left upper arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also saw the writing "White Eagles"?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes, because when he approached me with his big knife, which had blood on it, and when he threatened to slaughter me. However, my late wife, who died on the 15th of June, she tried to get something from my car. We had 3.800 Deutschemarks and some jewelleries from my wife and my daughter-in-law. Someone hit her on the head. We had some water. We threw some water until she regained consciousness, and then we proceeded towards the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kryeziu, but I'm afraid we'll have to continue at a faster pace, and you'll have to give me shorter answers because we are under time restrictions. I'd now like to ask you in relation to other testimony we've heard before this Tribunal, if you had seen people in black uniforms in your village?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: Yes, there were, but I can't say about that day. But until that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see on e-court Defence exhibit 6D126.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, I'd like to ask you something related to paragraph 2 of your statement and regarding your younger son Agron Kryeziu. That's the part of your statement that you corrected, or at least we received corrections. Here we have a statement by Ardijan Kumnova, who was a member of the KLA in Glodjane which had an admission centre of the KLA. And on page 3 of the B/C/S version and page 3 in English, of the draft translation in English, he mentions the men who were members of his group. And you will see on the screen in line 5 from the top, the name of Agron Kryeziu. The statement was given in 1998.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: May I answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. Can you tell us, please, is this true, that your son was a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please be asked not to speak at the same time as counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person should know that my son does not know where Gllogjan is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this person on the list is not your son, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And please, could the witness be asked to wait for the translation of the answer before answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu, the interpreters are asking me to ask you to pause until Mr. Lukic completes his question, and then leave a little time before you answer so that they can interpret the answer for the other languages listening. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown 6D127, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this another exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is one document. It's actually a diary or a war diary for Nazmi Brahimaj. [Interpretation] Can we please have on e-court page 7 of 6D127.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid we don't have the right page, the next one, if it could scroll down, please. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unlike the statement we saw previously, which covered year 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this page. Sorry, can we scroll up a bit on this page. Thanks. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see that the date is 22nd February 1999. And if you can see from the top, line 20 from the top, is the beginning of the sentence that reads: "There are certain problems with the administrative service because the soldiers were not issued with IDs," and the next sentence goes, "I suggest that Agron Kryeziu be assigned to positions in Lumbarda and that Brigade 131 should cover Dusanovo."

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that even this is not correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI KRYEZIU
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, I think we'll need to interrupt you if that's a convenient time to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Any time is good for break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that will be until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Kryeziu, we have to break now for the day and resume your evidence tomorrow; that will be at 9.00 in this courtroom. So you need to be back, ready to continue at that time. Meanwhile, it's very important that you have no discussion with anyone at all about your evidence, either the evidence you've given so far or the evidence you may get give in the case. Talk to whoever you like about whatever you like, but keep off the subject of the evidence. So could you please now leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall see you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the extent of tomorrow's business remains unclear at the moment. Once it is clear, you'll be notified. That may lead to some further discussions about Friday's arrangements behind the scenes, rather than waiting to discuss them in court tomorrow, but I can't tell you exactly how these arrangements will work out. So for the moment all I can do is adjourn until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25 ...
